summary: Four astronauts have arrived at the International Space Station following the fastest U.S. express flight to date, aboard a SpaceX launch that coincides with NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 preparing to conclude its station science mission. In civil space and science developments, NASA selected a team to explore a potential lunar cave and confirmed its Venus-bound DAVINCI probe can withstand extreme heat, while astronomers identified the lowest-mass double neutron star system discovered to date and modeled how water behaves on the moon. On the defense front, the U.S. Space Force officially retired a 1970s-era missile warning satellite constellation and selected two companies to build new space-to-space satellites by 2028, alongside a Department of Defense demonstration contract aimed at beaming solar power from space. Commercially and internationally, China launched its Guowang and Yaogan-40 satellites into orbit, launch provider Skyrora pushed its target orbital launch timeline to 2030, and satellite startups Satlyt and Foundational secured new capital rounds for orbital data networks and laser ranging technology. Looking ahead, readers should watch for the Space Development Agency’s scheduled launch of 21 additional data transport satellites next week.
